title: Quantum Weighted Moving Average for Predicting Limit Order Book Trends
authors: Matthias Kamm, Dinh-Long Vu, Patrick Rebentrost
abstract: Can quantum computers be useful for forecasting multivariate financial time series? In this work, we consider the problem of predicting price trends from limit order book (LOB) data. After identifying key components of classical models, we introduce the quantum weighted moving average (QWMA) model. The two main building blocks are, first, classically preprocessing via normalization of both feature and temporal dimensions and, second, a linear combination of unitaries-based layer for unitarily-embedded classical data. The models are evaluated on the FI-2010 benchmark dataset and a second dataset of China A-share stocks. While we do not present evidence of quantum advantage, the combined classical-quantum model demonstrates performances close to the best classical models. The quantum part of the model is expressive enough to focus on the most predictive parts of the time series. Several specializations of the QWMA model are considered, in particular a variant related to the widely-used exponential moving average (EMA). We give consideration to the limitations of the methods and the datasets.
summary: This work applies quantum machine learning techniques, specifically the Quantum Weighted Moving Average (QWMA), to predict financial trends from Limit Order Book data. The model combines classical data preprocessing with quantum unitaries to process time-series information. Although quantum advantage was not proven, the resulting hybrid model performs competitively with state-of-the-art classical methods.
main_problem: The paper investigates the feasibility of using quantum machine learning models to forecast price trends from complex, multivariate Limit Order Book (LOB) financial data.
main_result: While no definitive quantum advantage was shown, the combined classical-quantum model (QWMA) achieved performance comparable to the best classical benchmarks, suggesting the quantum component is highly expressive.
method: The approach involves classically preprocessing LOB data (normalization) before encoding it into quantum states via a Unitary Embedding, which is then processed by a Quantum Weighted Moving Average (QWMA) operator.
model_or_system: The core model is the QWMA, which is a quantum circuit structure based on a linear combination of unitaries (LCU). It is compared against simpler variants like QSMA and QEMA, using LOB data as the input time series.
key_observables: F1-score is the primary metric used to evaluate prediction performance across different datasets and model variants.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the number of qubits ($n_q$), the choice of unitary embedding circuit (e.g., Shallow, Circuit 1), and the weighting scheme (uniform vs. exponential).
main_assumptions: The authors note that the model requires post-selection for hardware implementation and that the comparison is limited by the choice of fixed context windows and embedding circuits.
figures_summary: Figures compare the F1-score of QEMA vs. QSMA across varying qubit counts and embedding circuits on different datasets, and illustrate the structure of the parameterized quantum circuits used for embedding.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QWMA model, details the classical preprocessing and quantum encoding steps, compares QWMA, QSMA, and QEMA performance on benchmark datasets (FI-2010, China A-shares), and analyzes the impact of normalization and weighting schemes.
why_interesting: The use of quantum circuits to process time-series data, even in a financial context, provides an interesting, albeit tangential, application of quantum circuit design principles that could inform quantum algorithms for sequential data processing.
